MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 10, 2024
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:01 p.m., on December 10, 2024, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on December 5, 2024, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Elaine Lister.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 pm Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 pm with all five City Council Members present.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

26. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as

City Council Minutes  6  December 10, 2024
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended the Sober Living and Recovery Task Force
Meeting on November 15 and stated that there has been movement on legislation that is coming in.
She asked Attorney Curley to speak on the Costa Mesa lawsuit and the end of her comments. Council
Member Bucknum said there will be a full report to the Council sometime in February. She attended
the Market Glow Feast, her regular OCCOG Meeting, and the Winter Gala at the Norman P. Murray
Center. She also participated in an event with Kurt Pringle and Associates at Ranch Saloon and will
be attending the ACCOC League of Cities tomorrow night. Council Member Bucknum gave kudos
to Trish on her State of the City and how the theme tied everything together that is going on in the
city. She spoke on the upcoming Mayors Conference in Washington D.C. and indicated that SCAG
is going to also be in attendance, and we will try to set up meetings on Friday with some of our
Representatives to talk about the Olympics and funding opportunities She announced that she and
her husband Paul will be Mr. & Mrs. Clause in Santa’s House this weekend and reminded residents
that on December 21 the Holiday Mix and Mingle and the Whoville Night Market. There will be
shuttles going back and forth from the Civic Center to the Night Market across the street. She wished
everyone a very Merry Christmas and ended her comments to say the reason for the season Isaiah
9:6 “for to us a savior is born”, and in Luke 1:14 “he will be a joy and delight to you, and many will
rejoice at his birth”.

City Attorney Curley commented on the City of Costa Mesa lawsuit. He said about a decade ago
Costa Mesa passed an ordinance regulating sober living homes. The owners of these home
contended that this was discrimination against people with disabilities. Recovering addicts were
considered disabled under federal statute and essentially were immune from regulations. This case
has been tied up in the court of appeals. The good news was the last of the appeals was determined
that this does not discriminate and that laws do not harm the handicap. To the contrary, it will ensure
that these facilities are actually providing safe and healthy proper services.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell gave kudos to all involved in the wonderful State of the City and
congratulated Mayor Kelley and Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch for a great year. He highlighted some
Olympic information, indicating that we have various interested parties looking to train in our city.
Council Member Goodell said we hosted a representative from Guam and the Secretary General of
the Oceana National Olympic Committee, and they are very interested in moving forward with
training camps starting next year in Mission Viejo for their swim teams, track and field teams, and
their battle sports teams such as Taekwondo, boxing, wrestling, etc. these camps would typically be
two to four weeks next summer.. He said we also hosted member of the Australian Swim and Dive
Team as well as their track and field teams today. Council Member Goodell also understands the
Swiss, Swedes, and Germans are looking for various locations to train in Southern California. He
stated the race is on to secure facilities for the 2028 Olympics for all these National Olympic
Committees and Sports Federations from various countries. He said there will be more updates as
we go into the new year.

City Council Minutes  7  December 10, 2024
 Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the Nadadores Holiday party and thanked Michelle Mitchell for
hosting a great party. She spoke about attending the No Lunch Lunch event at the Second Harvest
Food Bank and she couldn’t say enough about this organization. She stated that is a wonderful
organization that focuses on food insecurity. They have many ways that people can get involved
not just during the holiday season but year-round. There are volunteer opportunities for both young
and mature individuals from working in the warehouse or helping with their crops there is something
for everyone. For those interested, go to feedoc.org for more information.

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch highlighted the following events he attended. He attended the gift wrapping
even at Target where the sheriff’s department works with selected families to shop for gifts and staff
is available to wrap the presents for them. He stated it was very rewarding and always fun to see the
smiles. He announced that Santa’s Workshop concludes on the 22 and encouraged residents to bring
their children, grandchildren, or just want to get in the holiday spirit. He concluded that he was given
the opportunity to go out with OCFA on one of the helicopters to tour the burn areas as well as the
areas in the canyons that could have potential issues of fire risk as well as mud slides. We can be
hopeful for moderate rain, but we there if we do get a lot there will be problems. He commented
that the new Firehawk Helicopters can carry over a thousand gallons of water with a staff of three to
four inside. He hopes we never have to use them in Mission Viejo, but they are available if need be.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley highlighted the following events that she attended: Grand opening of Wendy’s on
Alicia Parkway, the new arcade at the Shops of Mission Viejo, Coffee with a Cop, and the Winter
Gala. She gave kudos to Director Mark Nix and staff for their oversight of the adoption of marine
families this Christmas. Close to 200 families were adopted by our Mission Viejo residents, the
Community of Character Committee, as well as Councilmember Bucknum. She stated it was
uplifting to see our city has been doing this for the last few years and to see all the boxes overflowing
with gifts at City Hall. Mayor Kelley thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and staff for
their hard work at Santa’s arrival. She mentioned that her family celebrates Christmas as the birth of
Jesus Christ our Savior. She wished everyone a Merry Christmas and a Happy Hanukkah season.
She concluded with asking for prayers for one of our police deputies that was badly hurt in a
motorcycle accident.

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

27. Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2025

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell to appoint Bob Ruesch
  to serve as Mayor in 2025.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
City Council Minutes  8  December 10, 2024
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell seconded by Mayor Kelley to appoint Wendy
  Bucknum to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2025.

  Council Member Vasquez announced she will nominate herself for Mayor Pro Tem. Mayor
  Kelley asked for a second to the motion. The motion died for a lack of a second.

  Council Member Vasquez asked that the following statement be part of the record:

  We are all equals on this dais.

  Each of us was duly elected, each holds an equal say, and each holds an equal share of the
  vote.

  So why am I being passed over?

  The roles of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem are ceremonial.

  What makes me unsuitable or less deserving of these roles?

  Historically, these positions have been rotated fairly among council members. Everyone else
  on the dais has been Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem.

  My long-serving colleagues have each been Mayor twice, and Mayor Kelley has been mayor
  six times.

  All fellow council members have served as Mayor Pro Tem one year and then as Mayor the
  next.

  Again, why am I being excluded from this tradition?

  I’ve been a dedicated public servant, missing only one meeting while still recovering from a
  week-long hospital stay.

  So why am I being skipped over?

  The decision to bypass me calls into question the integrity of this council, its professionalism,
  and its commitment to the community.

  It undermines not only the principles of fairness and tradition but also the trust placed in us by
  the community we serve.

  By excluding me, you are not just disrespecting me—you are disrespecting and disregarding
  the residents of District 3.

  Therefore, help me understand Why I Am Being Excluded.

City Council Minutes  9  December 10, 2024
   Mayor Kelley thanked Council Member Vasquez for sharing her thoughts and stated that there
  has never been a firm tradition of rotating the Mayors and Mayor Pro Tem’s.

  Council Member Bucknum stated that the last election changed a lot of traditions and values.
  She spoke about a previous Mayor that was appointed out of the abundance of being fair and
  that Mayor did not represent the values of the majority of the Council which resulted in major
  issues that created a nightmare for the entire year. She stated that things have happened over
  the years that have helped the Council to view things differently. Council Member Bucknum
  mentioned that in the last election the city moved to districts and four of those districts received
  50-60 percent of the vote. She stated that Council Member Vasquez received less than 41
  percent of the vote in her respective district. Council Member Bucknum then called for the
  vote.

  Council Member Vasquez stated that as equals on this dais, each Council Member has one-
  fifth of the vote and asked for clarification as to what specific things happened over the years.
  She stated that as a non-partisan body, the Council needs to behave as such. Council Member
  Vasquez stated she still has a seat on the dais regardless of the percentage of the votes she
  received, so that is a moot point. Council Member Bucknum stated that Council Member
  Vasquez did not get a second on her motion. Council Member Vasquez agreed she did not,
  which is why she made her statement and questioned the integrity of this Council. Council
  Member Bucknum responded that Council Member Vasques has been questioning the integrity
  of this Council since she was elected. Council Member Vasquez concluded that there is a lot
  to question and it’s a shame that some people feel that they need this kind of attention and that
  they need these positions to make their lives feel fulfilled.

  Mayor Kelley stated we have a call for the vote, so please register your votes.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell seconded by Mayor Kelley to appoint Wendy
  Bucknum to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2025.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None
